entities.rationale: Severe water stress, heat and a nuclear-armed neighbour drive collapse risk. Getting near-free essentials to 90% of 1.5 billion people needs superintelligence to cut water, sanitation and health costs drastically.
A capable state and cheap energy favour abundance under superintelligence. A Taiwan or US war, import blockades and very rapid aging are the main threats.
Rich, an energy exporter and the likely home of superintelligence, but health care alone costs well over 10% of income today. Great-power war or domestic conflict are the main collapse paths.
Peaceful and energy self-sufficient, but only 30% have safely managed water and coastal cities face sea-level rise, so abundance depends on very large cost drops.
Very weak political stability, Indus water stress, climate floods and nuclear rivalry with India make collapse a serious risk. Abundance is remote.
Insurgency, banditry, weak government and fast population growth threaten security and food. With 62% electricity access and 30% safe water, near-free access for 90% is far off.
Large food and energy surpluses make collapse unlikely outside global doom. High violence and inequality are the main obstacles to abundance.
A low-lying delta exposed to floods, salinisation and sea-level rise, with fragile politics. Strong recent health gains help, but near-free essentials need superintelligence.
Plenty of energy, land and food, but war with NATO, regime instability and nuclear risk make security the dominant collapse path.
Recurring civil wars, drought and famine risk make security and food the weak points. With 57% electricity and 14% safe water, abundance is very unlikely.
Cartel violence and severe water stress in the north and in Mexico City are the main risks, and only 43% have safely managed water.

Excellent governance and safety make it a strong abundance candidate with superintelligence. Heavy energy and food imports and regional war are its weak points, and extreme aging keeps health costs high.
Near-total dependence on the Nile, heavy wheat imports and high debt with a growing population make food and water the main collapse paths.
Typhoons, sea-level rise, energy imports and South China Sea tensions are the risks. Low safe-water coverage keeps abundance hard.
Chronic conflict, 40% undernourishment and the weakest institutions in the group make a nationwide security or food collapse likely. Abundance is a long shot even with superintelligence.
A stable, effective state developing fast. The Mekong delta's exposure to sea-level rise and tensions with China are the main risks.
Extreme water stress already threatening Tehran, war with Israel and the US, sanctions and a fragile regime drive a high collapse risk.
Middle-income with good health outcomes, but dependence on energy imports, rising water stress, earthquakes and regional conflict are the risks.
Rich, safe and well governed, so collapse mostly comes from global doom or a war with Russia. Essentials cost 27% of income today, so abundance needs superintelligence.
Good health and a food surplus, but coups, high water stress, energy imports and a sinking Bangkok are the risks.
